prompt: A TypeScript package has three internal parsers, but consumers need only `parseInvoice(text)`. Which surface best preserves representation freedom?

options.text: Export `parseInvoice`; keep parser representation private.
Export the parser barrel so clients can choose a stage when needed.
Expose parser objects so clients can tune parse stages.
Publish every intermediate type so consumers can reproduce parsing.

feedback.reason: Consumers need one operation; the parser representation is internal.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A narrow module export surface limits compatibility commitments.
details.scenarioApplication: Only `parseInvoice(text)` is named as a consumer requirement.
details.errorCorrection: Wildcard exports publish internal names without a client need.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Export additional types only when callers need to name them in the supported contract.
details.transfer: Expose the operation callers require and keep implementation structure replaceable.

messages.text: Publishing internal stages commits the module to names consumers do not need.
Mutable stage objects expose parser representation beyond the requested operation.
Reproducing the parser in clients defeats the package boundary.

prompt: The pricing module stores amounts as integer cents today, but consumers only need to request a quote and display the returned amount. What should be public?

options.text: Export quote behavior and a semantic amount value.
Expose cents and document the unit for consumers.
Expose the pricing row so callers can update it directly.
A mutable price singleton shared by every consumer.

feedback.reason: Consumers need pricing behavior and a returned amount, not storage internals.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An abstraction can preserve a stable result while internal representation changes.
details.scenarioApplication: The scenario states integer cents may change while caller needs stay fixed.
details.errorCorrection: Exposing the field makes a storage change into a consumer migration.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The amount contract must still define units/currency clearly.
details.transfer: Keep storage representation behind a stable client-facing contract.

messages.text: The prompt says storage representation may change; documenting cents still publishes it.
A persistence row exposes storage and write authority beyond quote display.
Shared mutable state makes updates and consumers’ observations ambiguous.

prompt: A library’s public function returns `VendorTimeoutError`, but clients do not otherwise use the vendor SDK. What API boundary reduces vendor coupling?

options.text: Map the vendor failure to a library-owned timeout/result contract.
Export the entire vendor error hierarchy.
Catch every vendor error and report success with an empty value.
Make clients import the vendor SDK to inspect private fields.

feedback.reason: Clients need a meaningful failure outcome without vendor details.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A library-owned error contract separates client semantics from provider representation.
details.scenarioApplication: The SDK is an internal mechanism and its error may change with upgrades.
details.errorCorrection: Returning success hides a real failure and changes semantics.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Preserve distinctions clients need; do not flatten meaningful outcomes.
details.transfer: Translate provider errors at the module boundary into supported library outcomes.

messages.text: Publishing the hierarchy makes the SDK part of the public compatibility surface.
An empty result falsely signals successful work.
Private vendor fields are not a stable client contract.

prompt: A module exports a `UserRecord` type that includes database table and cache-key fields. External callers need only a user ID and display name. What is the safer contract?

options.text: Export a client-facing user view with only the fields required by callers.
Export the database record unchanged because it is already available.
Let callers read cache keys and update the database directly.
Hide the module entirely even though external callers need user data.

feedback.reason: The persistence representation contains fields outside the stated client need.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A deliberate public view prevents internal storage details from becoming commitments.
details.scenarioApplication: Callers need identity and display data, not table/cache implementation fields.
details.errorCorrection: Exporting the record couples clients to storage evolution.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Include fields only when their semantics are stable and supported.
details.transfer: Separate the external contract from persistence models.

messages.text: Convenience of an existing type does not make its fields a supported API.
The prompt grants no need for cache control or direct persistence writes.
The stated callers do need a supported way to read user data.

prompt: An internal module has `normalizeForWire`, used only by one exported operation. Should consumers import it directly?

options.text: Keep it unexported and let the public operation use it internally.
Export it because it appears in the source file.
Re-export it through every package barrel.
Require callers to duplicate its normalization algorithm.

feedback.reason: The helper has no independent client requirement.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Non-exported module declarations are not visible outside the module in TypeScript.
details.scenarioApplication: One public operation is the only named consumer.
details.errorCorrection: Exporting the helper enlarges compatibility surface without benefit.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a second client needs the exact normalization contract, review whether it should be promoted.
details.transfer: Promote an internal helper only when an actual supported client contract requires it.

messages.text: Source visibility to the author does not imply package visibility.
Barrel re-export still makes the helper part of the consumer surface.
Duplicating normalization creates drift and is unnecessary.

prompt: A package exports a default `Client` class with six methods, while most consumers need only a small read operation. Which API change is most targeted?

options.text: Expose a read capability; keep unrelated methods for their clients.
Publish the full Client through a global singleton for convenient discovery.
Remove all exports so no package client can use it.
Expose the transport object to bypass the client class.

feedback.reason: A client’s needed operation should shape its usable contract.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A focused capability reduces consumer dependence on unrelated methods.
details.scenarioApplication: The scenario identifies a read-only consumer with no write need.
details.errorCorrection: A singleton adds lifecycle and shared state not requested.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not remove methods that existing supported consumers still use.
details.transfer: Design API surfaces around real client operations and compatibility needs.

messages.text: A singleton exposes unrelated methods and adds shared lifecycle state to a read-only client.
Other package clients still have supported operations; removing all exports exceeds this scope.
Transport is implementation detail, not the requested read capability.

prompt: A module has a stable exported `parse(text)` function and several internal parsing stages. A refactor changes those stages but not results. What compatibility promise is relevant?

options.text: Preserve the exported function’s documented behavior; internal stage names can change.
Keep every internal helper name unchanged for package clients.
Expose the stage graph so clients can coordinate with the refactor.
Treat any source edit as a breaking API change.

feedback.reason: Only the supported export is part of the client-facing contract.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Module encapsulation permits implementation refactoring behind unchanged behavior.
details.scenarioApplication: The parse result and exported signature remain stable.
details.errorCorrection: Requiring private helper stability blocks internal changes without a client contract.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If documented behavior changes, assess that public contract separately from implementation names.
details.transfer: Compatibility is defined by supported client-visible behavior and exports.

messages.text: Internal helper names are not public when they are not exported.
The prompt gives no client need for the internal stage graph.
A source change alone does not alter the public contract.

prompt: A TypeScript declaration file exports `InternalRow`, but its package documentation says no consumer should depend on it. What should the module do to enforce its intended surface?

options.text: Remove the export and expose only the stable consumer type.
Keep the export and rely on a warning in documentation.
Rename it with an underscore while leaving it exported.
Duplicate it under a second public name.

feedback.reason: The declaration currently makes the type importable despite the intended boundary.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A real module export is the technical visibility boundary; naming conventions alone do not hide it.
details.scenarioApplication: The type is explicitly intended to remain internal.
details.errorCorrection: Documentation does not prevent a consumer from importing an exported name.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A deprecation period may be needed if clients already depend on the exported type.
details.transfer: Align actual exports with the supported compatibility contract.

messages.text: A warning cannot technically stop imports or establish an internal surface.
An underscore does not remove the export.
A second name increases rather than reduces public commitment.

prompt: A module offers both `createReport(options)` and direct `Report` construction. Constructor callers can bypass required validation. Which surface protects the invariant?

options.text: Export the validated factory and keep direct construction internal.
Export both paths and document that callers should choose the factory.
Expose the constructor but make validation a private caller responsibility.
Remove validation and let each caller normalize independently.

feedback.reason: Direct construction bypasses the invariant that the module owns.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A factory can enforce required setup before returning a usable value.
details.scenarioApplication: The prompt says constructor callers can skip validation.
details.errorCorrection: Documentation alone leaves the bypass available.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Expose direct construction only if the type can preserve its invariant for every supported creation path.
details.transfer: Public creation paths should uphold the same validity contract.

messages.text: Two creation paths retain the known bypass.
The invariant belongs to the module, not every caller.
Caller duplication invites inconsistent validation.

prompt: A package barrel currently exports every file with `export *`; a newly added experimental parser becomes public accidentally. What change controls the package surface?

options.text: Replace the wildcard with an explicit list of supported exports.
Keep the wildcard and prefix experimental names with `internal`.
Ask consumers not to import the new parser.
Move experimental code into another folder but keep the wildcard.

feedback.reason: The wildcard automatically includes a new exported declaration.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An explicit entrypoint makes additions an intentional compatibility decision.
details.scenarioApplication: The experimental parser should not be a supported client API.
details.errorCorrection: A name prefix does not prevent importing an exported symbol.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A separate package is an option only if it has a real ownership or release boundary.
details.transfer: Make public exposure deliberate at the package entrypoint.

messages.text: Consumers can still import the exported prefixed name.
A request not to import it leaves the wildcard export unchanged, so it remains public.
Moving the file does not remove it from the wildcard barrel, so it is still exported.

prompt: A public `Result` union is used by clients to distinguish `notFound` from `forbidden`. An implementation adds a vendor response code to each variant. What should remain public?

options.text: Preserve both result variants; map vendor codes internally.
Expose each provider code as a required field on both variants.
Collapse both variants to `failed` because one provider status covers them.
Return the raw HTTP response to all callers.

feedback.reason: Clients rely on two meaningful library outcomes, not transport codes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The public contract should preserve caller-relevant distinctions while hiding mechanism detail.
details.errorCorrection: Adding required provider codes couples clients to one implementation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a provider code changes client action, add an intentional stable semantic field.
details.transfer: Translate transport detail without erasing contract distinctions clients use.

messages.text: Required vendor codes couple clients to implementation-specific representations.
The clients use `notFound` and `forbidden` as distinct outcomes.
Raw transport data exposes details beyond the supported result contract.

prompt: A function accepts `{timeoutMs?: number}`. Omission means use the module default; explicit `0` means no waiting. Which public type contract preserves that distinction?

options.text: Keep `timeoutMs` optional and document distinct omitted versus zero behavior.
Coerce omission and zero to the same default.
Make it required and force callers to copy the default constant.
Replace it with a boolean named `fast`.

feedback.reason: The caller-visible distinction between absence and a supplied zero is meaningful.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Optionality can encode whether a caller supplied a value when semantics define it.
details.scenarioApplication: Omission chooses the module default; zero has a separate behavior.
details.errorCorrection: Coercing both values destroys the stated contract distinction.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The implementation must preserve presence when interpreting the option.
details.transfer: Model only distinctions that the scenario says callers can observe.

messages.text: The two inputs are explicitly defined to behave differently.
Requiring all callers to know the default duplicates policy.
A boolean does not communicate the numeric timing contract.

prompt: A function’s public options object exposes the SDK’s `RetryOptions` type, which changes on every vendor release. What boundary keeps clients insulated?

options.text: Own stable retry options and map them to the SDK.
Re-export the SDK retry type from the package entrypoint.
Have every caller construct the vendor-specific retry object.
Remove retry configuration and silently use provider defaults.

feedback.reason: The public operation has its own supported retry needs.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A module-owned options type prevents a vendor release from changing consumer source.
details.scenarioApplication: The SDK type is volatile while the package owns the client contract.
details.errorCorrection: Re-exporting makes the SDK shape a transitive public dependency.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Retain a configuration field only if it has stable client semantics.
details.transfer: Keep provider-specific configuration translation inside the adapter.

messages.text: Re-exporting passes each vendor shape change directly to clients.
Each caller would need to track the SDK type and its releases.
Silently removing caller control changes supported retry behavior.

prompt: A module exports `setStatus(status: string)` even though only `pending`, `approved`, and `rejected` are legal. What public API expresses the supported inputs accurately?

options.text: A status type limited to the three supported values.
Any string plus runtime logging for unknown values.
A database row object so callers can assign arbitrary fields.
A numeric status whose mapping is undocumented.

feedback.reason: The supported input set is finite and explicit.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A narrow type communicates the accepted contract to callers and tools.
details.scenarioApplication: Only three values are stated as legal.
details.errorCorrection: Any string advertises unsupported inputs and defers preventable mistakes.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Runtime validation may still be needed at untrusted boundaries.
details.transfer: Keep type-level and runtime validation aligned at the API edge.

messages.text: Logging does not make unsupported values part of the contract.
The row object exposes storage shape and broader mutation power.
Undocumented numbers hide rather than express the meaning.

prompt: An exported class includes a `cacheKey` property used internally to optimize reads. No caller needs it. What is the better visibility choice?

options.text: Keep `cacheKey` private and expose only the stable behavior clients need.
Make it public because it may help advanced clients later.
Expose a setter so clients can tune the cache.
Move it into a public base class for reuse.

feedback.reason: The property is an implementation detail with no client requirement.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Private representation can change without forcing consumer compatibility.
details.scenarioApplication: No caller needs the cache key.
details.errorCorrection: Speculative future usefulness is not a present API contract.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a concrete client need appears, design a semantic capability rather than exposing an optimization key.
details.transfer: Do not turn internal optimization state into public representation.

messages.text: Public exposure creates compatibility cost without demonstrated value.
The prompt gives no supported client tuning requirement.
A public base class adds inheritance commitments for an internal field.

prompt: A consumer needs to report progress while a long import runs, but the importer currently exposes mutable internal phase objects. What contract is safer?

options.text: Expose a stable read-only progress contract.
Expose mutable phase objects so callers can update import state.
Ask callers to inspect private fields after each callback.
Publish every importer class so callers can subclass the workflow.

feedback.reason: The caller needs progress observation, not control of the import state machine.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A read-only API communicates observation without exposing mutable representation.
details.scenarioApplication: The needed client capability is to report progress.
details.errorCorrection: Mutation can let callers violate internal workflow invariants.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Add only progress fields with stable meaning across implementations.
details.transfer: Expose the smallest client capability and retain internal state-machine freedom.

messages.text: The client needs observation, not authority to mutate the importer state machine.
Private field inspection is not a stable supported contract.
Subclassing every importer class exposes far more than progress observation.

prompt: A package already supports `load(id)` and a new implementation can use a cache internally. No caller needs cache controls. What should the API change be?

options.text: Keep the exported `load(id)` contract and implement caching behind it.
Add cache policy, key, and eviction fields to every caller.
Expose the cache instance so clients can clear it directly.
Change the return type to the internal cache entry.

feedback.reason: The internal implementation changes while the client operation remains stable.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A stable exported API permits internal optimization without caller coupling.
details.scenarioApplication: Callers still ask to load by ID and need no cache behavior.
details.errorCorrection: Caller-supplied cache controls expose an implementation concern without a requirement.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If cache invalidation becomes a client guarantee, add a semantic operation then.
details.transfer: Do not widen a stable API solely because its implementation acquired a new mechanism.

messages.text: Those fields commit every caller to a cache strategy.
The cache instance exposes internal mutable state.
An internal cache entry is not the client’s result contract.

prompt: A module has one stable operation used by external callers and multiple internal implementations. Which export arrangement best supports changing the implementations?

options.text: Export the stable operation; keep implementations internal.
Export every implementation and require callers to choose one.
Let callers import whichever source file is newest.
Expose implementation fields through a shared mutable singleton.

feedback.reason: Consumers depend on one behavior while the implementations can vary.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A stable API separates clients from the module’s replaceable internals.
details.scenarioApplication: The scenario says external callers use one operation.
details.errorCorrection: Publishing all implementations makes each one a compatibility commitment.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Expose implementation selection only if callers have a stated supported choice.
details.transfer: Keep replaceable implementation details behind the stable client boundary.

messages.text: No client choice is stated; publishing each class expands the compatibility surface.
Source paths change with refactors and are not a stable client contract.
Shared mutable internals can interfere across callers and expose representation.
